lesson_1.title: Best Case Search
lesson_1.task: You are given an array and a target value. Implement a function find_best(arr, target) that checks only the first element of the array. If the first element matches the target, return index 0 immediately. If the array is empty or the target is not found at index 0, return -1. Do not perform any full traversal or loop through the array.

lesson_1.title: Worst Case Search
lesson_1.task: You are given an array and a target value. Implement a function find_worst(arr, target) that only checks the last element of the array. If the last element matches the target, return its index (last index). If the array is empty or the target is not at the last position, return -1. Do not scan or iterate through intermediate elements.

lesson_1.title: Constant Time Demo
lesson_1.task: You are given an array. Implement a function constant(arr) that returns the first element of the array regardless of its size. If the array is empty, return the string 'Empty'. The operation must be performed in constant time O(1) by directly accessing index 0 without iteration.

lesson_1.title: Linear Growth Demo
lesson_1.task: You are simulating execution steps in a program. Implement a function linear_growth(n) that simulates a loop running exactly n times and returns the total number of iterations performed. If n is less than or equal to 0, return 0.

lesson_1.title: Quadratic Growth Demo
lesson_1.task: You are simulating nested loops. Implement a function quadratic_growth(n) where both an outer loop and an inner loop run from 1 to n. Return the total number of iterations performed, which should equal n × n. If n is less than or equal to 0, return 0.

lesson_2.title: O(1) Lookup
lesson_2.task: You are given a list and an index. Implement a function lookup(arr, index) that returns the element at the given index using direct access. If the array is empty, the index is out of bounds, or invalid, return 'Error'.

lesson_2.title: O(n) Traversal
lesson_2.task: You are given an array. Implement a function traverse(arr) that iterates through all elements and returns the total number of elements counted. If the array is empty or None, return 0.

lesson_2.title: O(log n) Halving
lesson_2.task: You are given a number n. Implement a function halve_count(n) that repeatedly divides n by 2 until it becomes 1 or less. Return the number of valid divisions performed. If n is less than or equal to 0, return 0.

lesson_2.title: O(n²) Pairing
lesson_2.task: You are simulating pair generation using nested loops. Implement a function pairs(n) where both loops run from 1 to n. Return the total number of iterations performed, equal to n × n. If n is less than or equal to 0, return 0.

lesson_2.title: O(n+n) vs O(n)
lesson_2.task: You are comparing sequential loops. Implement a function double_loop(n) that runs two separate loops from 1 to n and returns the total number of iterations across both loops. If n is less than or equal to 0, return 0.

lesson_3.title: Array vs Variable
lesson_3.task: You are given an array of numbers. Implement a function running_total(arr) that iterates through all elements using a single accumulator variable and returns their sum. If the input is None or empty, return 0.

lesson_3.title: String Builder Growth
lesson_3.task: You are given a list of characters. Implement a function build_string(arr) that concatenates all elements sequentially and returns the final string length. If the array is empty or None, return 0.

lesson_3.title: 2D Array Allocation
lesson_3.task: You are working with a square matrix structure. Implement a function matrix_size(n) that returns the total number of elements in an NxN matrix representation. If n is less than or equal to 0, return 0.

lesson_3.title: In-Place Modification
lesson_3.task: You are modifying an array directly in memory. Implement a function in_place(arr) that doubles each element inside the same array and returns it. If input is None or empty, return an empty array.

lesson_3.title: Out-of-Place Creation
lesson_3.task: You are creating a new transformed array. Implement a function out_place(arr) that returns a new array where each element is doubled from the original. The original array must remain unchanged. If input is None or empty, return an empty array.
